contradiction_summary: The $36M figure in the original claim is real but mischaracterized. It appears in the ILR May 2024 primary report, but specifically as the peak median for PRODUCT LIABILITY cases in the single year 2022. The 10-year median (2013–2022) for ALL nuclear verdict case types is $21 million, and the auto-accident category (which encompasses trucking) also has a $21 million median over the same period. Preliminary 2023 data puts the overall median at ~$23.8 million. The claim as stated — '$36M median' for trucking-related nuclear verdicts — overstates the figure by ~70% when applied to the trucking/auto-accident category.
suggested_revision: Replace claim with: 'Nuclear verdicts (liability verdicts ≥$10M) in auto accident cases — which include trucking — carried a median of approximately $21M over 2013–2022, rising to ~$24M in 2023, per the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Institute for Legal Reform (May 2024). The $36M figure cited in some industry coverage refers specifically to the peak median for product liability cases in 2022, not to trucking cases broadly. Approximately one in four auto-accident nuclear verdicts involves a commercial trucking company.' [Source: ILR Nuclear Verdicts Report, May 2024, verified via PDF]
reasoning: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce Institute for Legal Reform May 2024 report is a primary, independently authored, publicly published research document verified via PDF download and markitdown conversion. It directly addresses nuclear verdicts with precise medians by case type and year. The original $36M claim is factually traceable to this document but is applied to the wrong case category — the trucking/auto-accident median is $21M (10-year) or ~$24M (2023). The corrected claim can be cited at High confidence using the ILR PDF as primary source.
